questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours and pipe B fills it in 15 hours. How long will both pipes together take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
A per hour = 1/10; B per hour = 1/15
Together = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6
Time = 6 hours

**Short Trick:** T = AB/(A+B) = (10×15)/(10+15) = 150/25 = 6 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and pipe B fills it in 12 hours. Both are opened together. How long to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
A per hour = 1/6; B per hour = 1/12
Together = 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4
Time = 4 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours. A leak at the bottom drains the full tank in 24 hours. If the tank is empty and the pipe is opened (with the leak), how long to fill?
questions.explanation:
Fill rate = 1/12 per hour
Drain rate = 1/24 per hour
Net rate = 1/12 − 1/24 = 2/24 − 1/24 = 1/24
Time = 24 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Inlet pipe A fills a tank in 8 hours, outlet pipe B drains it in 24 hours. Both are open. How long to fill the tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A and B fill a tank in 4 and 6 hours respectively. Pipe C drains it in 12 hours. All three are opened. How long to fill?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours. If the pipe runs for 3 hours, what fraction of the tank is filled?
questions.explanation:
Rate of A = 1/10 per hour
Work done in 3 hours = 3 × 1/10 = 3/10
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two pipes together fill a tank in 4 hours. One pipe alone fills it in 12 hours. How long does the other pipe alone take?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A (12 hrs) and B (15 hrs) are both opened. After 5 hours, B is closed. How many more hours does A take to fill the tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours. Due to a leak at the bottom, it takes 9 hours to fill. In how many hours will the leak drain the full tank?
questions.explanation:
Fill rate without leak = 1/6
Effective fill rate with leak = 1/9
Leak drain rate = 1/6 − 1/9 = 3/18 − 2/18 = 1/18
Leak drains full tank in 18 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A (12 hrs), B (8 hrs) and drain C (6 hrs) are all opened simultaneously. How long to fill the tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A and B fill a tank in 6 and 8 hours respectively. Both are opened together. After 2 hours, B is closed. How much total time to fill the tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A (10 hrs), B (15 hrs) and drain C (20 hrs) are all open. How long to fill the tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A full tank is being drained by two pipes A and B. A drains it in 10 hours, B in 15 hours. How long to empty if both are opened?
questions.explanation:
Combined drain rate = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6
Time to empty = 6 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Three identical pipes fill a tank in 4 hours. In how many hours will two such pipes fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
3 pipes fill in 4 hours → rate of 3 pipes = 1/4 per hour
Rate of 1 pipe = 1/12 per hour
Rate of 2 pipes = 2/12 = 1/6 per hour
Time = 6 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A (8 hrs), B (6 hrs) and drain C (4 hrs) pipes. A opens first for 2 hours, then all three open. How long is the total time to fill?
questions.explanation:
First 2 hours (A only): 2/8 = 1/4 filled
Remaining = 3/4
All 3 net rate = 1/8 + 1/6 − 1/4 = 3/24 + 4/24 − 6/24 = 1/24 per hour
Time for 3/4: (3/4) ÷ (1/24) = (3/4) × 24 = 18 hours
Total = 2 + 18 = 20 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank at 5 litres per minute. A leak drains at 1 litre per minute. If the tank capacity is 150 litres, how long to fill from empty?
questions.explanation:
Net fill rate = 5 − 1 = 4 litres per minute
Time = 150 / 4 = 37.5 minutes
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills in 4 hours. A is opened first. After 1 hour, B also opens. They finish together in 2 more hours. How long does B take alone?
questions.explanation:
First 1 hour (A only): 1/4 filled. Remaining = 3/4
A+B in 2 hours: 2 × (1/4 + 1/B) = 3/4
1/4 + 1/B = 3/8
1/B = 3/8 − 1/4 = 3/8 − 2/8 = 1/8
B alone = 8 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A (12 hrs) and B (15 hrs) are open. After 4 hours, a drain pipe C (60 hrs) also opens. How long total to fill?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A tank has an inlet filling in 6 hours and an outlet draining in 12 hours. Both are opened when the tank is empty. How long to fill?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A tank is 3/4 full. An inlet A fills it in 8 hours, an outlet B drains it in 12 hours. How long to fill the tank completely with both open?
questions.explanation:
Net rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24 per hour (filling)
Remaining to fill = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4
Time = (1/4) ÷ (1/24) = (1/4) × 24 = 6 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A (16 hrs) and B (12 hrs) fill a tank. Both are open. Due to a leak, the tank fills in 48/5 hours. In how many hours does the leak alone drain the full tank?
questions.explanation:
Without leak: 1/16 + 1/12 = 3/48 + 4/48 = 7/48
With leak: 1/(48/5) = 5/48
Leak drain rate = 7/48 − 5/48 = 2/48 = 1/24
Leak drains full tank in 24 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B together fill a tank in 12 hrs. B and C together fill it in 8 hrs. A, B and C together fill it in 6 hrs. How long does A alone take?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 20 hours. A is opened alone for 5 hours, then B is also opened. They fill the tank together in 3 more hours. How long does B alone take?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A cistern has a capacity of 60 litres. Pipe A fills at 3 L/min, B fills at 2 L/min, and C drains at 1 L/min. All three are opened together. How long to fill from empty?
questions.explanation:
Net fill rate = 3 + 2 − 1 = 4 litres per minute
Time = 60 / 4 = 15 minutes
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
